record.paper_title: Resolving Open Problems on the Euler Sombor Index
record.context_brief: maximum Euler Sombor index for connected graphs with fixed order and girth
record.original_question: Let EUS(G) = sum over all edges v_i v_j in E(G) of sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j), where d_i and d_j are the degrees of the endpoints. For connected graphs G with a fixed order n, where order means the number of vertices, and a fixed girth g, where girth means the length of the shortest cycle, determine the maximum possible value of the Euler Sombor index EUS(G) and characterize all connected graphs that attain that maximum.

evidence.quote: The Euler Sombor index (EU S) of a graph G is defined as EU S(G) = Σ_{v_i v_j ∈ E(G)} sqrt(d_i^2 + d_j^2 + d_i d_j).

The standard notations used in this article are as follows: C_n, P_n, and K_n denote the cycle, path, and complete graph of order n, respectively. The girth of a graph refers to the length of its shortest cycle.
However, some key problems remain open: determining the maximum EU S index and characterizing the extremal graphs among connected graphs with fixed order and given girth

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph $G=(V,E)$, let $d_v$ denote the degree of vertex $v$. Define the Euler Sombor index of $G$ by
$$\mathrm{EUS}(G) \;=\; \sum_{v_iv_j \in E(G)} \sqrt{d_i^{\,2} + d_j^{\,2} + d_i d_j}.$$
The order of $G$ is $|V(G)|$, and the girth of $G$ is the length of a shortest cycle in $G$ (defined for graphs containing at least one cycle).

Fix integers $n \ge 3$ and $g$ with $3 \le g \le n$. Let $\mathcal{G}_{n,g}$ denote the class of all connected graphs of order $n$ and girth $g$.

Determine
$$\max_{G \in \mathcal{G}_{n,g}} \mathrm{EUS}(G),$$
and characterize all graphs in $\mathcal{G}_{n,g}$ that attain this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on the Euler Sombor index has settled the minimum of EUS over connected (and unicyclic) graphs with fixed order and girth, and has resolved several related extremal problems (fixed pendant vertices, chemical unicyclic graphs, given diameter). However, the maximization version for connected graphs with fixed order and given girth, together with the characterization of the extremal graphs, is still flagged as an unresolved problem in the most recent literature on this index.

status_evidence.title: Resolving Open Problems on the Euler Sombor Index (arXiv:2507.17246)
status_evidence.snippet: The paper resolves the minimum of EUS for unicyclic and connected graphs with fixed order and prescribed girth, but the maximization version for connected graphs with fixed order and girth is listed among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Maximum EUS over connected graphs with fixed order and girth remains open.

status_evidence.title: Extremal unicyclic and bicyclic graphs of the Euler Sombor index
status_evidence.snippet: Determines extremal unicyclic and bicyclic graphs for EUS but not the general connected case with fixed girth.

status_evidence.title: Maximal tree and unicyclic graph for Euler Sombor index with given diameter
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses maximization for trees and unicyclic graphs with given diameter, not connected graphs with given girth.
status_evidence.claim: Related maximization results exist but do not cover the present problem.
